verdict.rationale: Smithery has its own programmatic surfaces suited to unattended use: a REST interface for connecting to MCP servers, a CLI that can add connections and call tools, API-key and service-token auth, and automatic token refresh without manual intervention. However, nothing documents headless or CI usage explicitly, so CI suitability is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit CI/headless documentation (e.g. pipeline examples or GitHub Actions), documented non-interactive CLI auth via env vars or API keys, machine-readable output flags, and independent hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Smithery gives you a simple REST interface for connecting to MCP servers.
smithery tool call <connection> <tool> [args]  # Call a tool
smithery mcp add <url>                  # Add an MCP server connection
Resources within a namespace can be managed by anyone with the appropriate API key scoped to that namespace
